original_question: Construct explicit approximately Hadamard matrices A with entries in {-1, 1} such that c sqrt(n) ||x||_2 <= ||Ax||_2 <= C sqrt(n) ||x||_2 holds for all x in R^n, while guaranteeing that the distortion ratio C/c is small.
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.1 ("Approximately Hadamard Matrices"), read together with the Section 9 defining paragraph and the constructive existence result in Theorem 9.1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target area in the paper: approximately Hadamard matrices with entries in {-1,1}, the defining two-sided Euclidean norm inequality c sqrt(n) ||x||_2 <= ||Ax||_2 <= C sqrt(n) ||x||_2 for all x in R^n, and the key optimization goal that the ratio C/c should be small.
missing_details: The paper is asking for a family of matrices A_n, one for each dimension n >= 1, not just a single unspecified matrix A.
The constants c and C are meant to be universal/absolute: 0 < c < C < infinity should be independent of n and of x.
The point of the open problem is not bare existence; existence is already known, and the paper asks for nice/simple explicit constructions.
The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: A_n is a real square matrix in {-1,1}^{n x n}, acting on R^n with the Euclidean norm ||.||_2.
What must be small is a provable uniform upper bound on the ratio C/c across the whole family, not merely in one dimension or in an unspecified asymptotic sense.
The immediate context includes Theorem 9.1, which already gives a constructive circulant example via flat Littlewood polynomials; the open problem itself does not impose a circulant restriction.

No homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or characteristic assumptions are relevant here; the stand-alone formulation instead needs the missing quantifiers over n and x and the independence of c, C from n.
refined_question: For every integer n >= 1, can one find many nice/simple explicit constructions of real n x n matrices A_n in {-1,1}^{n x n} such that there exist absolute constants 0 < c <= C < infinity, independent of n, with c sqrt(n) ||x||_2 <= ||A_n x||_2 <= C sqrt(n) ||x||_2 for all x in R^n, and with a provably small absolute upper bound on the ratio C/c?
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because Section 9 introduces approximate Hadamard matrices through exactly this two-sided l_2 inequality, explains that existence is already known, records in Theorem 9.1 a constructive circulant family, and then states Problem 9.1 as the search for many nice explicit constructions with guaranteed small C/c. The rewrite therefore keeps your core inequality and +/-1-entry condition, while adding the missing universal quantifiers, the real square-matrix setting, and the paper’s actual emphasis on explicit constructions rather than another abstract existence statement.
